items.title: Email addresses section
items.description: The email addresses on an account: which one is primary, which are verified, add another, make one primary or remove it, each step explained in the row.
items.docs: Controlled: keep emails in state and update it in each callback. Every callback may return a promise; the row shows a busy state and a rejection is shown in words. Throw an Error with a message from onAdd to explain why an address was refused; the other callbacks show a general message. items.title: Public profile section
items.description: Edit how others see you: picture, display name, @username with a live availability hint, bio with a counter, links, and a preview that updates as you type.
items.docs: profile is the saved profile; the draft lives inside until Save, and a new profile passed back replaces it. onSave receives the cleaned-up draft and, when a new picture was chosen, the File to upload as the second argument (profile.avatar of a new picture is only a temporary preview address: store the real URL you get back). onCheckUsername(username) resolves true when the name is free and is only asked for names that follow the rules and differ from the saved one.

items.name: appearance-settings
items.title: Appearance settings
items.description: Choose how the interface looks: three theme preview cards, a density choice with a live sample list, and an optional font choice, all applied at once.
items.docs: Controlled: keep value in state, update it in onChange and apply theme, density and font yourself. The theme previews paint their own palette, so each one is true on any page theme. Leave systemTheme out and System reads the browser; pass fonts={[]} to hide the font choice.

items.title: Accessibility preferences
items.description: The settings people reach for first: text size with a live sample, motion, contrast, underlined links and keyboard hints, each applied at once.
items.docs: textSize is an index into TEXT_SIZE_STEPS (from steps.ts): apply its scale to your root font size. motion and contrast are plain values for a data attribute or a CSS variable; applying them is yours. Leave systemMotion out and Follow system reads prefers-reduced-motion from the browser.

items.name: language-region-section
items.title: Language and region section
items.description: Language, country, time zone and formats in one card, with a live sample line showing the date, time and number exactly as they will read.
items.docs: value is the saved setting; the draft lives inside until Save, and a new value passed back replaces it. The preview is formatted with Intl from the draft, always with a time zone, at a fixed moment (sampleDate, a date or an ISO string) so server and browser render the same text. languages are written in their own names; timeZones are IANA ids, grouped by their offset at that moment; locale is the language the country names are shown in.

items.name: privacy-settings-section
items.title: Privacy settings section
items.description: Who can see your profile and what you share: visibility as choice cards, then switches for activity, search and analytics, each saying what it changes for others.
items.docs: Controlled: keep value in state and set it in onChange. Changes apply at once; return a promise from onChange and the status line shows Saving, then the confirmation or an error. Applying the settings (who may read the profile, robots tags, analytics) is yours.

items.title: Connected accounts
items.description: The sign-in providers linked to an account: who is connected, as whom and since when, with connect and disconnect per row and a guard on the last way in.
items.docs: An account counts as connected once it has an identity or a connection date. Without canDisconnect, the only connected provider is protected; pass your own rule when a password or passkey also counts as a way in. protectedHint says how to add another way in: a tooltip on the protected provider, and plain text under the row on touch screens and in narrow rows where a tooltip cannot open. Dates are shown in the timeZone you pass (default UTC) so server and browser agree.

items.name: data-export-section
items.title: Data export section
items.description: The right of access without a support ticket: pick what to include and a format, request the export, and follow earlier ones by status and expiry.
items.docs: Data in, callbacks out: pass the groups, the earlier exports and onRequest. While an export is preparing (or onRequest is pending) the button rests and the card says it will email the person; add the new export to `exports` with status "preparing" and flip it to "ready" with a size, expiresAt and href when it is done. Dates use the locale and timeZone props (UTC by default); pass `now` to pin the relative "Expires in 5 days". title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: billing-details-section
items.title: Billing details section
items.description: What appears on invoices: company, address, a tax number checked for format and live, billing emails as chips and a reference, saved as one block.
items.docs: onSave may return a message (shown by the Save button), an object of messages keyed by field (shown against the fields), or nothing. onValidateTaxId resolves true or false for the live "Valid" or "Could not verify"; it runs once the number has the right shape. taxIdLabels adds or changes a country's label, example and pattern over the built-in table in tax-ids.ts. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: email-preference-center
items.title: Email preference center
items.description: The page behind 'manage your emails': a frequency per list, a pause for 30 days, and unsubscribe from everything behind one inline confirmation.
items.docs: Works without a signed-in session: pass the address (it is shown partly masked) and save each change from onChange, which may return a promise. A list's frequencies default to Off, Weekly and Monthly. Up to four steps sit side by side (on a phone, long labels become a menu) and more than four are always a menu. The value "off" is what Unsubscribe from everything sets. Leave out onPause, onResume or onUnsubscribeAll to drop that part of the page. Controlled with value, or uncontrolled with defaultValue. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: workspace-profile-section
items.title: Workspace profile section
items.description: A workspace's name, URL, default time zone and language, with a live preview of the address, a warning before links change and a save that lights up.
items.docs: The slug is limited to lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens as you type. onCheckSlug resolves true when an address is free; it is asked after a pause in typing and only for an address that differs from the saved one. Changing the slug shows a warning in words before saving. timeZones takes IANA names, listed in the order you pass them, and languages takes { value, label } pairs; both lists are searchable (a language is also found by its name in `locale`, so "German" finds Deutsch) and have sensible defaults in defaults.ts. While Save runs the fields are locked. Pass the saved workspace back as `workspace` after onSave and the form follows. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: branding-settings
items.title: Branding settings
items.description: How a workspace looks to its customers: logos for light and dark, an icon and a brand colour with a contrast check, and live page and email previews.
items.docs: Images are URLs: onUpload receives the chosen file (only SVG and PNG get that far) and resolves to the address it can be shown from, and Save hands back the same four values. An address that turns out not to draw is taken back with a message, so a broken image is never saved. The colour is checked against white and black text (minContrast 4.5 is WCAG AA, 7 is AAA) and against a white page; one that fails is not applied and the reason is shown. colors sets the swatches. The previews are drawn on literal white, because they show the customer's page, not your product. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: authenticator-setup
items.title: Authenticator setup
items.description: Two-step sign-in setup in one card: scan the QR code or type the key, then confirm with the first six-digit code. It works without a camera.
items.docs: The block draws no QR code: pass your own SVG or image in qr (draw it from the otpauth address with a QR library). It is wrapped with alt text that carries the key, so setup works without a camera, and it sits on a white tile, so keep it dark on light. onVerify resolves true or false; a wrong code is announced and cleared. After success the card shows what you pass as next, usually a button to the recovery codes, and the focus moves to that confirmation so the button is one Tab away. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: recovery-codes-section
items.title: Recovery codes section
items.description: Recovery codes shown once with copy, download and print, and a checkbox people must tick to confirm they saved them before they can continue.
items.docs: Codes of any length work: they sit two to a row while the longest fits and one to a row when it does not. Pass plain strings for fresh codes, or { code, used } to show which were spent (they are struck through and read Used). With onContinue the block asks for "I have saved these codes" and keeps Continue locked until it is ticked; with onRegenerate a new set is offered behind an inline confirmation, and the new codes come back through `codes`. Print hides everything on the page except a plain sheet of the unused codes. Without onDownload the block saves recovery-codes.txt itself. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: transfer-ownership-card
items.title: Transfer ownership card
items.description: Hand a workspace to another member: pick the new owner, read what changes, and confirm by typing the workspace name in a dialog that names what you are giving away.
items.docs: members are the people you would allow as the new owner; a member with disabledReason is listed but cannot be chosen. onTransfer(memberId) may be async: resolve to nothing when it worked, or resolve to (or throw) a message when it failed, and the card keeps the choice and shows it. Leave consequences out for a default list that names the new owner, and confirmDescription out for the default dialog text; say what is true for your product in both. onCancel adds a Cancel button for flows the person can leave.

items.name: early-access-features
items.title: Early access features
items.description: Let people opt into previews: each feature with an Alpha or Beta badge, a switch, what changes and how to undo it, and links to give feedback.
items.docs: Controlled: keep features in state and update enabled in onToggle. Return a promise from onToggle and the switch moves at once and stays busy until it settles; if it rejects, the switch goes back and the row says so. effect and undo are the words shown after a switch is turned on. A feature with disabledReason is locked and says why in text.

items.name: bulk-select-menu
items.title: Bulk select menu
items.description: The header checkbox with a menu for choosing what to select: all, none, unread, starred, with the mixed state and the count in words.
items.docs: Controlled: derive state (none, some or all) from your own selection and keep the selection in your callbacks. The checkbox runs onSelectAll when nothing is selected and onSelectNone otherwise. Each criterion shows the number it would select and is disabled at 0. After every choice a polite message says what was selected.

items.name: copy-as-menu
items.title: Copy as menu
items.description: Copy the same thing in the format the next tool wants: a split button whose menu offers Markdown, JSON, cURL or plain text and remembers the last choice.
items.docs: Each format's serialize() runs only when someone copies in that format, and may return a promise. Pass format and onFormatChange to keep the last choice yourself (in local storage, say), or defaultFormat to leave it to the button. Picking a format in the menu copies in it at once. Set as on a format when it reads badly after Copy as: "plain text" for Plain text. Formats carry functions, so build them in a client component.

items.name: add-to-calendar-button
items.title: Add to calendar button
items.description: Adds an event to the calendar people use, Google, Outlook, Apple or an .ics file, built from one event object with the time zone handled.
items.docs: A start without an offset (2026-11-12T19:00) is read in the event's timeZone; a Date or a string ending in Z or +01:00 is an exact moment. Give end or durationMinutes (default 60). All-day events take a date, and end is the last day. buildIcs, buildGoogleUrl and buildOutlookUrl are pure functions in calendar.ts that return null for an event that cannot be read. Pass uid so an edited event updates the first one in the calendar.

items.name: directions-button
items.title: Directions button
items.description: Get directions in the maps app people use: Apple Maps on iPhone, Google Maps elsewhere, Waze if they prefer, and the address to copy as a fallback.
items.docs: Give the destination an address (with its name, so the pin is labelled) or latitude and longitude; a name alone is not enough and disables the button with the reason. Without apps, Apple Maps comes first on iPhone and iPad and Google Maps elsewhere, decided after mount. Waze only drives. The link builders in directions.ts are pure and return null for a place that cannot be used.

items.name: save-contact-button
items.title: Save contact button
items.description: Save a person or business to the address book: it builds a vCard in the browser from one contact object and downloads it, with no server involved.
items.docs: The file is a vCard 3.0 with escaped text, lines folded at 75 octets and labelled phone, email and address types. On an iPhone it opens the Add Contact sheet. The accessible name adds who it is for, and a contact without a name disables the button with the reason. buildVCard in vcard.ts is pure and returns null without a name, so the same text can become a QR code.

items.name: follow-button
items.title: Follow button
items.description: Follow, Following and Requested in one button: optimistic, with a follower count, a clear way to unfollow and a rollback message when the request fails.
items.docs: Controlled: keep status and count in state and update both in onFollow and onUnfollow before they resolve. The button answers at once and rolls back with a message if the promise rejects; presses are ignored while a request is pending. Resolve onFollow with "requested" when the account needs approval, or pass isPrivate to ask for it up front; unfollowing a private account asks once. defaultStatus leaves the status to the button, and the count then stays as given for that starting status and moves with the button. The error line is wider than the button and widens the control with it, so where you right-align the button pass className="items-end" (or sm:items-end) and it keeps its right edge when a request fails. The accessible name stays "Follow <name>" and aria-pressed carries the state, while the visible word changes to Following or Requested.

items.title: Follow button demo
items.description: A working preview of Follow button.

items.name: like-button
items.title: Like button
items.description: A like button where the count is the point: it answers at once, rolls the number, plays one quiet ring and tells screen readers the exact count.
items.docs: Controlled: keep liked and count in state and update both in onToggle once the request has succeeded; the button already shows the new state while it waits, and rolls back with a message if onToggle rejects. defaultLiked leaves the state to the button, and count then stays as written for that starting state and moves with the button. Counts above 999 abbreviate by locale (1.2K, 1,2 Mio.) while the accessible name and the tooltip keep the exact number. Pass names to make the tooltip read "Liked by ...", and any @rhs-ui/icons glyph as icon: it is drawn filled once liked.

items.name: like-button-demo
items.title: Like button demo
items.description: A working preview of Like button.

items.name: vote-buttons
items.title: Vote buttons
items.description: Up and down arrows around a score for questions, answers and feature requests: one vote each, changeable, with the score announced.
items.docs: Controlled: keep value and score in state and update both in onVote once the request has succeeded. onVote receives "up", "down" or "none" (pressing the chosen arrow again clears the vote). The control moves the score by the right amount while the request is on its way, including two for a switch from down to up, and puts both back with a message in a bubble beside the control (to the right of a vertical one, to the left of a row, whichever side has room) if onVote rejects. score is written for the vote the control starts in. Set subject to name what is voted on, and allowDownvote={false} for a single arrow with a count.

items.name: vote-buttons-demo
items.title: Vote buttons demo
items.description: A working preview of Vote buttons.

items.name: watch-button
items.title: Watch button
items.description: A watch button with levels: all activity, mentions only or nothing, as a split button whose words and bell always say what you will be told.
items.docs: Controlled: keep level and count in state and update both in onLevelChange once the request has succeeded. The main button switches between the last level that was on and "ignore"; the chevron opens a radio menu. Pass levels to change the words (id must stay all, mentions or ignore) and subject for the accessible name ("Watching this issue, all activity"). The count moves by one when watching starts or stops. A rejected onLevelChange rolls everything back with a message.

items.name: watch-button-demo
items.title: Watch button demo
items.description: A working preview of Watch button.

items.name: approval-buttons
items.title: Approval buttons
items.description: Approve and Reject as one decision: a reason when rejecting, who decided and when, and a short window to change your mind.
items.docs: Uncontrolled it runs by itself: Approve and Reject call onApprove and onReject (each may return a promise and shows its own busy and error state), then the status line takes over with Change decision for undoWindow seconds. Controlled, pass status, decidedBy, decidedAt and reason, and set status back to pending in onChangeDecision. Reject always asks for a reason first (requireReason makes it required). Pass locale and timeZone so the time reads the same on the server and in the browser. A decision made here shows just the time on the day it was made and adds the date on any other day; a time you pass in decidedAt always carries its date, so a page rendered on the server reads the same once it has loaded. In a narrow space Change decision drops under the sentence. The control holds no form of its own, so it can sit inside yours, and Ctrl or Cmd with Enter confirms a rejection.

items.title: Approval buttons demo
items.description: A working preview of Approval buttons.

items.name: social-sign-in-buttons
items.title: Social sign-in buttons
items.description: Continue-with buttons for sign-in providers: monogram marks instead of brand logos, a last-used tag first in the list, and one busy state.
items.docs: Pass providers (id, label and an optional mark) and onSelect(id). While onSelect runs, that provider's button shows a spinner and the others disable; a rejection puts a message under the list. For a redirect flow pass busy yourself. lastUsed moves a provider first and tags it. The default marks are neutral monogram tiles built from the name (GH for GitHub, G for Google, one letter more when two would match), so no trademarked logo ships; bring your own with mark. In a narrow row the name moves up against its mark so it still fits. layout is stacked, grid or icons (square buttons with a tooltip); the list is labelled for screen readers.

items.name: translate-toggle
items.title: Translate toggle
items.description: Translate a review or comment and back to the original with one quiet control that shows loading, translated-from and failed states.
items.docs: Nothing is translated unless you pass onTranslate(text), which returns the translated string and runs only when the control is pressed; the result is kept, so going back and forth asks once. Uncontrolled it manages its own state. To control it, pass state with onStateChange, and translation once the state is translated. sourceLocale and locale are the language codes that mark each version with lang, so screen readers switch voice. labels changes the words of the control for a site that is not in English.

items.name: use-location-button
items.title: Use location button
items.description: A Use my location button that handles every outcome in words: finding you, found with its accuracy, blocked, unavailable and timed out.
items.docs: navigator.geolocation is called only when the button is pressed, never on load. onLocate receives latitude, longitude and accuracy in metres and nothing is sent anywhere; onError receives denied, unavailable or timeout. Where the Permissions API exists, a site that is already blocked says so before the first press. The button renders nothing where there is no geolocation. Pass geolocation to supply your own source (a native shell, or a stub to try every outcome), and labels to change the words.

items.title: Use location button demo
items.description: A working preview of Use location button.

items.name: keep-awake-toggle
items.title: Keep awake toggle
items.description: A switch that keeps the screen on for recipes, scripts and slides with the Wake Lock API, taking it again after a tab switch.
items.docs: The lock is requested when the switch is turned on, requested again when the tab becomes visible (browsers let go of it while a tab is hidden) and released when it is turned off or the page goes. Nothing is requested on load: a switch that starts on (defaultOn or on) asks for the lock at the first touch or key press. If the browser refuses, the switch returns to off, onChange(false) is called and one line says why. Where the Wake Lock API does not exist the component renders nothing. Pass wakeLock to supply your own source.

items.name: listen-button
items.title: Listen button
items.description: Listen to this article with the browser's own speech: play, pause and stop, a choice of speed, and the sentence being read highlighted.
items.docs: Pass text, or targetRef for an element whose text is read sentence by sentence (the sentence being read is highlighted with the CSS Custom Highlight API, without touching your markup; mark anything that should not be read with data-listen-skip). lang picks the voice and how sentences are cut. The button reads in sentences, which also avoids Chrome stopping long utterances, and stops when the page is hidden or unmounts. Progress is shown as sentences, not time. A page has one voice: pressing a second button stops the first, and if anything else cuts the speech off the button goes back to rest. Where the browser has no speech synthesis it renders nothing; pass engine to supply your own.

items.name: reaction-bar
items.title: Reaction bar
items.description: Emoji reactions under a message or comment: counts, your own pressed, who reacted on hover, and an add button with a palette you walk with arrow keys.
items.docs: Keep reactions in state and update it in onToggle (applyReaction does the bookkeeping). The bar shows your press at once; if onToggle rejects it puts the count back and says so in words, and a request in flight blocks a second press on the same emoji. users lists the other people who reacted, so the tooltip can read 'You, Ana Reyes and 2 others'; it may hold only the first few names. max is the most different reactions one message can carry. disabled makes the bar read only: the chips keep full contrast, their tooltip and their place in the tab order (they are aria-disabled, not disabled) and only the add button is dimmed.

items.name: inset-sidebar-shell
items.title: Inset sidebar shell
items.description: An app frame with the sidebar on the page background and the page as a bordered, rounded surface beside it, scrolling on its own under a breadcrumb header.
items.docs: Pass your navigation as nav (a SidebarNav is itself the navigation landmark), the account button as footer, and breadcrumbs and actions as header. The page scrolls inside the surface, so the sidebar never moves. Below md the sidebar opens as a left sheet from the menu button and closes when a link is followed. Below lg only the last breadcrumb stays, because the header has no room for a trail that would shrink to a few letters. The first pixels of a scrolled page fade under the header; at rest nothing fades, so padded={false} suits a full-bleed table. The shell is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className. Pass linkAs for your router link and mainId when the page already uses id=main.

items.name: inset-sidebar-shell-demo
items.title: Inset sidebar shell demo
items.description: A working preview of Inset sidebar shell.

items.name: top-nav-shell
items.title: Top navigation shell
items.description: An app frame with the navigation along the top: brand, links with the current one marked, search, actions and account, then the page in a container.
items.docs: Pass links with currentHref (the current link gets aria-current) and your router's Link as linkAs. search, actions and account are slots: from md (or lg, see collapse) they sit in the sticky header, and below that width the links, the search and the actions move into a sheet opened from the menu button while the account stays in the header. pageHeader takes the PageHeader props and is drawn at the top of the content. collapse sets where the row takes over from the menu: md (default) fits four short links next to a labelled action, and five links need collapse="lg" (they want about 820px). With the default, a SearchTrigger shrinks to its icon between md and lg so the row never crowds. The menu closes by itself if the window grows past that width, and the search fills the menu whatever width class it carries. The header gets its bottom border once the page scrolls, measured with an IntersectionObserver. width sets the container to 72rem (default), 80rem or the whole width. Five areas or fewer fit the row; beyond that use a sidebar shell.

items.name: settings-shell
items.title: Settings shell
items.description: A settings layout: grouped side navigation, a page title and a focused content column, with the nav becoming a scrolling tab row on phones.
items.docs: Pass groups (labelled lists of links, the SidebarNav shape) with currentHref, plus title, description and actions for the page. backHref adds a Back to app link. The children are the sections of the page: they are stacked with one gap in a column of at most 42rem. From md the navigation sticks under the top of the viewport; on a phone the groups become a row of links that scrolls sideways with faded edges and the current page is scrolled into view. Pass linkAs for your router link.

items.title: Settings shell demo

items.name: filter-rail-shell
items.title: Filter rail shell
items.description: A layout for any list narrowed by filters: a rail of filter groups, a results toolbar, removable chips, an announced count and a sheet on phones.
items.docs: filters is a list of groups ({ id, label, activeCount, children }): the shell draws them as collapsible sections, in the rail from lg and in a sheet below it, and never renders both copies at once so no id or label exists twice. chips are the active filters ({ id, label, onRemove }); onClearAll drives Clear all in the row and Clear in the sheet; after Clear in the sheet focus moves to Show N results, so it never leaves the dialog. resultCount is shown, announced politely when it changes (from the page, or from the sheet while it is open, since a modal hides the page from screen readers) and written on the sheet's Show N results button. toolbar holds your sort and view toggle. open and onOpenChange control the sheet if you need to. Keep the filter state in the page, the shell holds none of it.

items.name: wizard-shell
items.title: Wizard shell
items.description: The frame for a multi-step task: a top bar with save and exit, a step rail, the step content and a sticky footer with Back and Continue.
items.docs: Pass steps ({ title, description }), the current index and onContinue; you decide what comes next in your own state. titleAs makes the step heading an h1 (the default, because the step is the page) or an h2. The step's heading takes focus whenever current changes (never on first render), so the new step is announced; finished steps in the rail call onStepChange. Set canContinue to false with canContinueReason and the footer shows that sentence instead of a dead button; on a phone it gets a row of its own above the buttons. onContinue may return a promise: the button shows a spinner until it settles, and errors are yours to handle inside it. onSkip adds Skip for now, onExit adds Save and exit, help is a slot in the header. The last step's button says Finish unless you set continueLabel. The step fades in when it changes (not under reduced motion).

items.name: dashboard-shell
items.title: Dashboard shell
items.description: A dashboard frame with named areas: a header with filters, a KPI strip, a main area, a side column and a full-width table zone.
items.docs: Fill the areas you have: kpis, main, side and table are slots, and an empty one leaves no hole (main takes the full width when there is no side). From lg they sit in four columns, below it in reading order. filters is the content of a bar under the title (a period picker, quick filters) that sticks to the top from md up and scrolls away on a phone; updatedAt adds Updated 2 minutes ago, on a row of its own on a phone, written as a full date on the server and turned relative in the browser, with locale and timeZone. Every area is a labelled region; rename them with labels. loading shows a skeleton in each area you filled. Charts are yours: drop them into the slots. Set --sticky-top when a fixed header sits above.

items.name: focus-shell
items.title: Focus shell
items.description: A distraction-free frame for one task: a minimal header, a single centred column, a quiet footer and a clear way out.
items.docs: brand sits left in the header and exit (a link back or a close button) right; a ghost Button there is pulled out by its own padding so its text ends on the margin. The column is 24rem (narrow), 32rem (default) or 44rem (wide); align is center or top. footer takes the legal links and language the language switcher. The page is min-h-dvh, never a fixed 100vh: the column is centred with auto margins while there is room and starts at the top when there is not, so the page scrolls normally on a short screen or with the keyboard open. A skip link points at the one main landmark (mainId).

items.name: mobile-tab-shell
items.title: Mobile tab shell
items.description: A phone-first app frame: a top bar with title and back, scrolling content and a bottom tab bar that respects the home indicator.
items.docs: Give it a title, three to five tabs ({ id, label, icon, badge }) and the id of the active one. Tabs are real links with aria-current: pass onTabChange to switch screens in state, or leave it out and give each tab an href. The title is large at the top of the content and moves into the app bar once it has scrolled out of view; onBack adds a back button, actions fills the right of the bar, fab floats a round button above the tab bar. The content scrolls on its own with overscroll-contain and ends where the tab bar begins. screenKey (default the active tab) says when the screen has changed: the content then starts at the top and fades in, and the new title takes focus so the change is announced (never on the first render, and not when a tab was pressed, which keeps its focus). The bar clears the notch and the home indicator with env(safe-area-inset-*). From md up the screen is 390px wide and centred; pass a height in className to size it.

items.name: rail-panel-shell
items.title: Rail and panel shell
items.description: A two-level app frame: a slim icon rail for the areas, a panel with the pages of the one you are in, and the content beside them. The panel folds, or opens as a sheet on phones.
items.docs: Pass areas ({ id, label, icon, badge }), the id of the active one and onAreaChange; switch panel (usually a SidebarNav) when the area changes. Each area is a button named for screen readers and in a tooltip, the current one carries aria-current and a filled tile. The panel folds with the toggle at the foot of the rail: panelOpen and onPanelOpenChange control it, or leave them out and the shell keeps it. Below md the panel is a sheet that opens beside the rail when you press an area (pressing another area while it is open switches it in place; an area without a panel opens nothing), closes when you follow a link or press the toggle, and gives focus back to the button you pressed. brand and railFooter fill the top and the foot of the rail, panelActions sits beside the panel's heading. The shell is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className. Pass mainId when the page already uses id=main.

items.name: section-sidebar-shell
items.title: Section sidebar shell
items.description: Two-tier navigation: the sections of a product along the top, and a sidebar that lists the pages of the current section only. Sheet and scrolling tabs on phones.
items.docs: Pass sections ({ id, label, href }), the id of the active one, sidebars (the pages of each section in the SidebarNav shape, by section id) and currentHref; the current section is underlined with aria-current, the current page is marked in the sidebar. Pass your router's Link as linkAs: both the sections and the pages use it, so switching section is a normal navigation and focus stays on the link you used. A section without an entry in sidebars has no sidebar. brand and account fill the header; sidebarFooter sits under the sidebar and in the sheet. Below md the sidebar is a left sheet opened from a menu button (focus returns to it, following a link closes it) and the sections scroll sideways under the brand with faded edges. The header never moves and the page scrolls inside the shell, which is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className. menuLabel, sectionsLabel, pagesLabel and skipLabel translate the words. Pass mainId when the page already uses id=main.

items.name: record-page-shell
items.title: Record page shell
items.description: The frame for one record, an order, a contact or a ticket: back link, title with status, actions, tabs, and a main column beside a details rail.
items.docs: Give it backHref (and backLabel, the list's name, which is read as 'Back to Orders'), the record's title (the page's h1; pass titleAs="h2" inside a preview), a status, a meta line, actions, and the two columns: main and rail. tabs, activeTab and onTabChange come as a set: the tabs scroll sideways with faded edges when they do not fit, and the main column is the tab panel of the current one, so put that tab's content in main. rail takes a DescriptionList with layout="stacked" (or anything); it is a labelled aside with railTitle as its heading, sticky from lg and under the main column below it. meta takes one node or a list of nodes set off with dots. The shell renders on the server unless you pass tabs; pass your router's Link as linkAs. It adds its own page padding: pass className="p-0" when your app shell already pads.

items.name: inspector-shell
items.title: Inspector shell
items.description: A list or table with a detail panel that opens beside it when a row is picked, with previous and next, and turns into a sheet on phones.
items.docs: Put the list or table in children and a search, filters or buttons in toolbar. Keep the selected record and open in your own state: set open when a row is picked, give the record's details as panel and its name as panelTitle, and answer onOpenChange(false) by closing. onPrevious and onNext walk the list: leave one out at the end and its button dims but keeps focus, so stepping with the keyboard never loses its place; leave both out for no buttons. Opening moves focus to the panel's heading (once the person has used the page: a panel that opens by itself on load does not take focus), Escape or the close button closes it and gives focus back to the row you pressed last (so put a real button or link in each row; a press elsewhere in the row counts as a press on its first one), and a change of record while open is announced. The panel opens by animating its width in 200ms, instantly under reduced motion. Below lg it is a sheet from the right with a focus trap; labels translates the words. The shell is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className.

items.name: summary-aside-shell
items.title: Summary aside shell
items.description: A two-column flow layout: the steps on the left and a sticky summary card on the right, which becomes a bottom bar with a sheet on phones.
items.docs: Put the steps or the form in children, the order, booking or quote in summary, and give the total already formatted (the shell does no arithmetic). action is the primary button: it is shown in the card, in the bottom bar and in the sheet, so give it form="your-form-id" and no id of its own. From lg the summary is a 22rem card that sticks under the header while the steps scroll; below lg a bar fixed to the bottom shows the total, the action and a Show summary button that opens the whole summary in a bottom sheet. The bar and the sheet respect the safe-area insets, and the steps get matching bottom padding so the bar never covers the last field. Changes of the total are announced politely. The steps are the main landmark (pass mainId when the page already uses id=main) and the card is a complementary one. header is a sticky bar for your mark and a note about secure payment; totalNote adds a line under the total, labels translates the words. The page scrolls like a normal page.

items.name: feed-shell
items.title: Feed shell
items.description: Three columns for community and social apps: navigation on the left, a narrow centre feed with a sticky header, and widgets on the right.
items.docs: Pass nav (three to five { href, label, icon, badge, badgeLabel } entries; badgeLabel says what the count is about, "new" by default) with currentHref and your router's Link as linkAs, a header (the feed's title) and the posts as children. From md the navigation is a list in the left column with brand, primaryAction and account around it; below md it is a bottom tab bar that clears the home indicator, and primaryAction floats above it (it is rendered once, in the same place in the page). tabs, activeTab and onTabChange come as a set: equal tabs under the title that stay on screen with it, and the posts of the current one go in children. widgets fills the right column from xl and follows the feed below it. The page itself scrolls, not a box inside it, so scroll restoration, find in page and the back button behave as on any page. The shell renders on the server unless you pass tabs; pass mainId when the page already uses id=main.

items.name: workbench-shell
items.title: Workbench shell
items.description: A tool layout with an explorer, canvas and inspector you can resize by mouse or keyboard, a toolbar, a status bar and sheets on phones.
items.docs: Pass canvas, and any of explorer, inspector, toolbar and status. The panels are separated from the canvas by drag handles that are also keyboard separators: focus one and press the arrow that moves it toward the canvas to grow its panel by 16px (Shift for 64), the other arrow to shrink it, Home to collapse it and End to bring it back. A double click on a handle brings its panel back to its starting width. Dragging a panel below half its minimum collapses it, and dragging out of the collapsed hairline opens it again. Two toggles in the toolbar collapse and restore the panels, and when the shell is narrower than 64rem (lg) they open the panels as sheets instead; breakpoint changes that width in rem, and it is never less than the panels' minimums and the canvas minimum need together; below it the panels are also hidden by CSS before the script has run, so a narrow screen never paints a squeezed layout first. The content of a panel is mounted once and moved between the panel and its sheet, so a field keeps what was typed and a tree keeps its open folders when a sheet closes or the shell crosses the breakpoint. The shell reads its own width, not the window's, so it works inside a pane, and it follows dir="rtl". The explorer and inspector scroll on their own; the canvas takes the room that is left, scrolls on its own, has min-width 0 so a wide editor or artboard can never push the layout out, and is a tab stop only while there is something to scroll. defaultSizes takes { explorer, inspector, collapsed } in px, minSizes the least width of the panels and of the canvas, and onSizesChange hands you the same shape once per gesture (a released drag, a key, a toggle; not a gesture that ends where it began), so it can go straight to localStorage and back into defaultSizes. Pass sizes to keep the layout yourself. When the shell is too narrow for the sizes you chose, the panels give way together and return to your sizes when it grows again. The toolbar slot sits between the toggles and scrolls sideways if it does not fit; status is a 28px strip that scrolls on a phone. The shell is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className.

items.name: map-panel-shell
items.title: Map panel shell
items.description: A full-bleed map or any view with a floating search and results panel that becomes a bottom sheet with three snap heights on phones.
items.docs: Pass canvas (your map: Leaflet, Mapbox, MapLibre, an image, a floor plan; the block draws nothing and loads nothing), panel (the results list), and optionally search, filters and controls. From 48rem of width the panel floats at the start (the left) as a 24rem card, with a tab on its edge that hides it and a Show results button that brings it back; controls sit in the opposite corner, and the layout follows dir="rtl". Below that it is a bottom sheet with three snap heights: peek (the search only), half and full (a strip of the map stays above it, and the controls fold away until the sheet is lowered). Move it by dragging the handle, with ArrowUp and ArrowDown, Home and End on the handle, by tapping the handle, or with the button beside the search. The sheet is not modal: nothing dims the map, nothing traps focus, and the map keeps taking input around it. In the tab order the panel comes first, then the controls, then your map. At peek the filters and the list step out of the tab order, and focusing the search lifts the sheet to half. open and onOpenChange control whether the panel is shown; snap and onSnapChange control the sheet's height (defaultOpen and defaultSnap leave it to the shell). The search slot sits in a 2.25rem row, which is what peek shows. The filters wrap onto more rows on the card and scroll sideways on a phone, with a fade at the end that has more to see; give every chip an icon, as a selected chip swaps it for a check, so selecting never changes its width. The shell is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className.

items.name: notification-item
items.title: Notification item
items.description: One notification row: who did what to which thing, when, an unread marker in dot and word, and the actions that apply.
items.docs: Put the rows in a ul. Pass actor ({ name, image }), verb, target ({ label, href }) and time. unread adds a dot, the word Unread for screen readers and a heavier title, and onMarkRead shows a check button on unread rows. The row is one link or button laid under its content: href makes it a link, onOpen makes it a button (or runs on the link, with the event so a router can call preventDefault), and the actions you pass stay separate tab stops above it. When the check button leaves with the unread state, focus goes to the row's link instead of falling to the page. Without now the time starts as a date and clock time and turns into "4 min. ago" once the page is live, then keeps itself current; pass now to get relative text in server HTML, in tests and in previews. The row follows its own width: actions sit beside the text from 28rem and under it below that. An icon beside an actor sits on the corner of the avatar; without an actor it replaces the avatar, and a bell stands in when neither is given.

items.name: comment-item
items.title: Comment item
items.description: One comment with author, role, time, an edited note and a body that folds, with reply, edit and delete. Nest replies to compose a thread.
items.docs: Pass author ({ name, image, href }), createdAt, body and, for a role next to the name, badge. editedAt adds an Edited note beside the time. actions lists what this viewer may do: reply is a button under the body, and edit and delete appear in an overflow menu, so give them only on the viewer's own comments. onAction receives the action; a delete runs it only after the person confirms in the comment itself (focus goes to Keep it, Escape cancels), and if it returns a promise the button waits, and if the promise rejects the comment says so and stays. Bodies of more than six lines fold behind Show more, a button that only exists when there is something to unfold; a plain string keeps its line breaks. For editing, set editing and put your own editor in body: it is shown in full and the actions step aside, and when editing ends focus goes back to the menu button. highlighted frames the comment a permalink points at and sets aria-current; give it an id so the link can find it. Replies are children: pass more CommentItems with size="sm" and they nest along a thread line. footer sits next to Reply, for a reaction bar. Without now, times start as a date and clock time and turn relative once the page is live.

items.name: message-bubble
items.title: Message bubble
items.description: A chat bubble for people talking to people: own and other styles, grouped corners, a reply quote and a send state.
items.docs: Put the bubbles in a plain block, in order; each brings its own spacing, tight inside a run and wider between runs. side is own (right, primary surface) or other (left, muted); position says where the bubble sits in a run from one person (single, first, middle, last) and squares off the corners that touch their neighbours, so work it out from the neighbouring messages. time is written as a clock time in locale and timeZone under the last bubble of a run, with the exact moment in its tooltip; every bubble keeps its time for screen readers. For your own messages status shows in words as well as a mark: Sending, Sent, Read, and Not sent with a Retry button when you pass onRetry. A failed message shows its state wherever it sits in a run, and pressing Retry hands focus to the line that then says Sending. replyTo quotes the message being answered, attachments draws images or files inside the bubble above the text, and author adds the avatar at the end of a run and the name at its start. Long words and URLs wrap, and line breaks in a string are kept.

items.name: task-row
items.title: Task row
items.description: A task as a list row: checkbox, title, due date in words, assignee, priority mark and subtask count.
items.docs: Put the rows in a ul. task is { id, title, href, done, completedAt, due, assignee, subtasks, priority }; the due date comes from DueDateLabel, so a date-only string such as "2026-10-28" is a calendar day and the words are Due today, Due tomorrow, Due in 5 days and Overdue by 2 days, with an icon and weight as well as colour. onToggle receives the state the checkbox asks for: update task.done, and set completedAt to have a finished task say Done on 12 Oct. The checkbox is its own control and never opens the task; completing it strikes the title and says Completed to screen readers. The rest of the row is one link (task.href) or button (onOpen) under the checkbox and the actions slot. A long title stays on one line in a wide row and takes up to two in a narrow one; the whole of it appears in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. selected marks the task whose details are open with a bar and aria-current; density="compact" tightens the rows. The row follows its own width: from 36rem everything sits on one line in fixed columns, below that the details wrap under the title. Pass now for deterministic due dates in tests and previews. Give the actions a group-hover/task-row class to reveal them on hover.

items.name: task-card
items.title: Task card
items.description: A compact card for a board or grid: title, label chips, due date, assignee stack and subtask progress, ready to be dragged.
items.docs: Put the cards in a ul. task is { id, title, href, cover, due, done, completedAt, assignees, subtasks }, labels are { id, label } chips above the title. The whole card is one link (task.href) or button (onOpen) with a ring around all of it on focus, and footer controls sit above it as their own tab stops. The card is a plain li that spreads every prop and the ref, so a drag library (dnd-kit, pragmatic-drag-and-drop) can wrap it; dragging gives it a firm border, a shadow and a small rise, selected a firm outline and aria-current. TaskCardSkeleton is the same card as a placeholder, with cover to reserve the image. items.name: project-card
items.title: Project card
items.description: A project at a glance: name, status, a progress line, team avatars and due date, as one clickable card with a menu.
items.docs: project is { id, name, description, status, progress, members, due, completedAt, icon, href }; status is planning, active, on-hold, completed or archived and is written in words with its own mark. The card is one stretched link (project.href) or button (onOpen) with a ring around all of it on focus; the star toggle (starred and onStar) and the overflow menu (menu, a list of { id, label, icon, destructive, onSelect }) are separate controls above it, so pressing them never opens the project. An archived project is dimmed by its surface and its tile rather than by opacity, so it stays readable. The tile shows icon, or the first letter of the name. ProjectCardSkeleton is the same card as a placeholder. It sizes to its column, so it works in any responsive grid. The due date comes from DueDateLabel; a completed project shows Done on 12 Oct from completedAt instead, and an archived one shows no date, so a finished project never reads as overdue. Pass now for deterministic words in tests and previews.

items.name: member-row
items.title: Member row
items.description: A team member as a list row: avatar, name and email, a role you can change, a status that includes pending invites, and a menu of actions.
items.docs: Put the rows in a ul. member is { id, name, email, image, role, status, invitedAt, owner } and roles is a list of { value, label, description }. Pass onRoleChange to make the role a select: it receives the new role and the member and may return a promise, in which case the select shows the choice while it runs, goes back and says so if it rejects, and the change is announced ("Sofia Rossi's role is now Admin."). An invited member reads "Invited 3 days ago" with Resend and Revoke in the menu, a suspended one can be restored, owner fixes the role and gives the reason (a tooltip on a wide row with a pointer, plain text on a narrow one and on a touch screen), and isYou adds a You tag and leaves out every destructive action. The menu fits the status unless you pass actions, and onAction reports the choice: Remove and Revoke only report, so confirm them in your own dialog. onRoleChange must update member.role by the time it resolves, because the change is announced then. The row reads its own width: it folds into two lines in a narrow container, and below 26rem the invite words move to a line of their own so the address stays readable. Pass now to get the relative time in server HTML; dates use locale and timeZone.

items.name: integration-card
items.title: Integration card
items.description: A connected tool on a settings page: status in words, what it syncs, the last sync, and connect or disconnect with a confirmation and a retry.
items.docs: integration is { id, name, description, mark, syncs, account, lastSyncedAt, problem, consequence } and status is connected, attention or disconnected. The status is written as a sentence first (Connected as anna@studio.nl, Needs attention with the problem, Not connected) and the badge only repeats it. onConnect and onDisconnect may return promises: the card shows a busy state until they settle, and a rejection keeps the card where it is with the reason and a Try again button, and the result is announced. Disconnect asks in an alert dialog; consequence names what stops, or a default line about syncing is used. busy and error let you track a request yourself. A card fills its grid cell and keeps its buttons on one line, so cards with different amounts of text stay level; in a card narrower than 24rem Configure becomes the gear alone, with the word as its name. The last sync reads "12 minutes ago" once the page is live; pass now to fix it.

items.name: event-chip
items.title: Event chip
items.description: A calendar event small enough for a grid cell: a bar, the time and a title, in timed, all-day and multi-day styles, with a +3 more companion.
items.docs: event is { id, title, start, end, allDay, calendar, tone, tentative } and variant is timed (a bar and the start time), all-day or multi-day (a filled chip); it defaults from event.allDay. Tones are four steps of the page's own ink (ink, graphite, stone, mist): change the TONES table to use your brand's hues. The chip is one button whose name reads "Design review, 10:00 to 11:30, Studio", so colour is never the only signal, and a tooltip shows the whole title when it is cut. dense draws the 20px chip for a month grid and keeps that height inside a flex or grid column. For a multi-day event draw one chip per week row, place it with a grid column span, and set continuesBefore and continuesAfter where it carries on. OverflowChip is the "+3 more" under a crowded cell. Times use locale and timeZone.

items.description: A working preview of Event chip.

items.name: week-strip
items.title: Week strip
items.description: Seven days in a row for choosing a day on a phone: weekday and date, today ringed, dots for days with events.
items.docs: value, defaultValue, min, max and marked use calendar days written as 2026-10-26, so they never shift with a time zone. marked is a list of days (one dot each) or an object that maps a day to how many events it has (up to three dots, and "has 3 events" in the day's name). The row is one tab stop: arrow keys move between days and choose as they go, Home and End go to the ends of the week, and Page Up and Page Down change the week; onWeekChange receives the first day of the new week. weekStart is 1 (Monday) by default and 0 is Sunday. Weekday names, the month and the full dates come from locale; today comes from the browser's clock in timeZone, or from the today prop. A page that is cached or built ahead of time must pass today: without it the first week drawn comes from the clock of whoever renders it, and a visitor after the week turned hydrates with a different week than the HTML holds. hideNav drops the month and the arrows, for a header of your own.

items.name: feature-gate
items.title: Feature gate
items.description: A locked-feature panel: the real content dimmed and inert behind a clear message and one upgrade action.
items.docs: While locked, the children stay where they are, muted and inert (the inert attribute and aria-hidden), and a panel on top is a labelled region with the plan in a badge, a title, a description and one action: a button, or a link when it has an href. Unlocked, the children are rendered as they are and keep their state; if the panel's button had focus, focus moves to the gate, and the unlock is announced. There is no blur and no gradient, on purpose. The panel reads the gate's own width: a stacked card in a narrow gate, and from 36rem a single-row bar with the lock, the words and the action, so a short feature still shows behind it. The gate is as tall as its children, or as the panel when that is taller.

items.name: activity-entry
items.title: Activity entry
items.description: One activity as a sentence: who, what, which object and the from-to change, with a time and an icon.
items.docs: Put the entries in a ul. actor is { name, image, system }: a system actor, a bot or a job, has a square tile with the icon instead of an avatar. The sentence is the actor, the verb, the object (a link when it has an href, cut to one line with the full name in its title) and the change, drawn as two quiet chips around an arrow, with "from" and "to" for screen readers so the row reads as one string. The time reads 12 minutes ago, yesterday, 3 days ago and then the date, with the exact moment in its title; pass now to fix it. On a narrow row the time drops under the sentence.

items.name: time-tracker
items.title: Time tracker
items.description: A start, pause and stop timer for time tracking that keeps true elapsed time even when the tab sleeps.
items.docs: The tracker is controlled: keep running, startedAt and accumulated yourself, in state, a store or localStorage. onStart receives the moment to store as startedAt, onPause the total in ms to store as accumulated, and onStop the total and the description. The elapsed time is accumulated plus the time since startedAt, read from the clock and never counted, so it stays right after the tab sleeps, the machine suspends or the page reloads. The display uses tabular numbers and the seconds are never announced: screen readers hear "Timer started", "Timer paused at 12 minutes" and "Timer stopped. 12 minutes recorded.". descriptionLabel adds a text field for what you are doing. formatClock and formatWords are in time-tracker/time.

items.name: checklist-card
items.title: Checklist card
items.description: A titled checklist with a progress count, strike-through on done items and an add row, for launch and packing lists.
items.docs: items is a list of { id, label, done, note }. onToggle receives the id and the state asked for, onAdd the trimmed text of the add row (Enter adds) and onRemove the id; leave a callback out and its control is not drawn. The count and the bar come from the items, progressLabel changes the words ("{done} of {total} packed"), and when everything is checked the count reads "Everything is checked". hideCompleted folds checked items away behind a button, controlled or with defaultHideCompleted. Each item is a checkbox with its own label in a labelled group; checking, adding and removing are announced, and removing an item, or checking one while the checked items are folded away, moves focus to its neighbour.

items.name: note-card
items.title: Note card
items.description: A note as a card: title, a clamped preview, last edited time, a pin and a label, ready for a notes grid.
items.docs: note is { id, title, preview, editedAt, href, labels, code }. The card is one stretched link (note.href) or button (onOpen) with a ring around all of it on focus; the pin (pinned, onPinChange) and the menu (a list of { id, label, icon, destructive, onSelect }) sit above it as separate controls. A pinned note says "Pinned" in its footer as well as in the icon. Labels are { name, tone } with four tones, the name is always written out, and past maxLabels they fold into "+2". A note with no text shows "No content yet", code switches the preview to a monospace face, and NoteCardSkeleton is the loading state. Cards fill their grid cell, so a grid keeps equal heights.

items.name: inbox-row
items.title: Inbox row
items.description: A message list row: sender, subject, snippet, time, unread and starred states, labels and an attachment mark.
items.docs: Put the rows in a ul. message is { id, sender, image, subject, snippet, time, unread, starred, attachment, labels, href }. The whole row opens the message (a link with href, a button with onOpen) and sits under the checkbox (onSelect, selected) and the star (onStar), which are separate controls. An unread message is set heavier, has a dot and says Unread to screen readers. density is comfortable (three lines, with an avatar) or compact (one line from 42rem wide, two below it); showAvatar overrides the default. The time reads as a clock time for today, the weekday for the last six days and then the date; pass now to fix it.

items.name: typing-indicator
items.title: Typing indicator
items.description: Who is writing right now, in words and three pulsing dots, handling one, two or many people and speaking up politely at most once every few seconds.
items.docs: Pass people as the list of names writing right now; the sentence follows it: Anna is typing, Anna and Tom are typing, Anna, Tom and 2 others are typing. max is how many names are spelled out (default 2) and one person too many is always named, so and 1 other never appears. label is the activity after is or are (default typing, or replying, or recording a voice message). With nobody writing the line fades out and keeps its height, so the thread above never jumps. The drawn line changes at once; the spoken copy is a polite status that waits announceEvery milliseconds (default 4000) between announcements. labels translates is, are, and and others.

items.name: reply-summary
items.title: Reply summary
items.description: A "5 replies, last reply 2 hours ago" link with a small avatar stack that opens the thread, for message and comment lists.
items.docs: Put it under a message or comment. replies is the count (fewer than one draws nothing), repliers the people who replied, most recent first, of whom three are drawn, and lastReplyAt when the latest came in. With href the line is a link, without it a button; onOpen receives the click, so a client-side router can call preventDefault() and navigate itself. The whole line is one control named like View thread, 5 replies, 2 new, last reply 2 hours ago. unread is true for a plain New or a number for 2 new, always written as text. A count of 1000 or more compacts to 1.3k on the line and stays 1,284 in the name. The relative time is read once and never ticks; pass now to get it in server HTML, in tests and in previews, and locale and timeZone for the language and the zone of the date shown before the clock is known. The line reads its own column: narrow, the time is written short (2h ago) and the hover swap to View thread goes; narrower still the third avatar, the second and the chevron step aside, and if even that is too much the time drops to a second line. The time is never cut off. labels translates every word.

items.name: help-launcher
items.title: Help launcher
items.description: A floating Help button that opens a short menu of docs, contact options, keyboard shortcuts and system status, with no third-party script.
items.docs: Mount it once near the root of the app. items is the menu in order: each entry has a label, an optional description and icon, and either an href or an onSelect, plus an optional shortcut shown as keys (display only: bind the key yourself) and a group, since a rule separates one group from the next. An href that starts with http opens in a new tab and shows an arrow. It is a real menu button: arrow keys move, Escape and a click outside close it, and focus returns to the button. position is bottom-right or bottom-left, label renames the button, heading adds a line above the entries, and open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control it. It keeps off the screen edge and the notch with safe-area insets; offset lifts it by any CSS length to clear a tab bar or a cookie banner. hidden draws nothing, for a page where it would cover content. contained positions it inside the nearest positioned ancestor instead of the browser window. It loads no third-party script.

items.name: call-log-row
items.title: Call log row
items.description: A call in a log: caller, direction as a drawn arrow and a word, time and duration, with a voicemail, a note and a call back button.
items.docs: Put the rows in a ul. call is { id, name, image, number, direction, at, duration, voicemail, note }: direction is incoming, outgoing or missed, duration is in seconds, and voicemail is { duration }. A caller without a name leads with the number, written for the locale (bare numbers are grouped, +1 numbers as (415) 555-0132; a number that already has spaces or dashes is shown as written; for exact national formats pass formatted text), and says Not in contacts. A missed call is marked by its word, a heavier name and a broken arrow as well as its colour. The row reads as one sentence, Missed call from Anna de Vries, 14:32, and Call back Anna de Vries is a button of its own: onCallBack may return a promise, and the button shows a spinner while it runs; if it rejects, the row says Could not call Anna de Vries. Try again. in a short alert under the line (labels.callFailed), and each press of the button is announced, also a repeat on the same person. onOpen makes the whole row a button under the others. onNote adds a note button, showNote prints call.note under the line, onPlayVoicemail draws a play button beside the voicemail length, and playSlot replaces it with your own player. Pass now to get Yesterday in server HTML; times use locale and timeZone (en-GB gives 14:32). The row reads its own width: narrow, the time sits beside the name, the length joins the arrow and the number gives way; the note button then gives way to onOpen.

items.name: chat-header
items.title: Chat header
items.description: The top of a conversation: avatar or group mosaic, name, presence or member count, and call, search and info actions.
items.docs: Put it above the thread. conversation is { id, name, image, group, members, memberCount, onlineCount, muted }: a group without an image is drawn as a mosaic of up to four members. presence is { state, lastSeenAt } for a direct chat and gives Active now, Away, Last seen 14:02 (or yesterday, Mon, 12 Oct) or Offline; a group counts its members instead, 12 members, 3 online. status replaces the line with your own words. The avatar and name are one button when onOpenInfo is passed, named Open info for Anna and described by the status line. The status is also a polite status of its own that speaks only once a change has held for a moment, and never when another conversation opens. actions are icon buttons with tooltips: a wide bar keeps maxInline (default 3), a narrow one keeps two, and the rest wait in a More menu. onBack shows a back button on a narrow bar only. muted adds a bell with a line through it and the word Muted. Pass now to get Last seen in server HTML; times use locale and timeZone. labels translates every word.

items.name: sla-timer
items.title: SLA timer
items.description: Time left on a service target: on track, at risk or breached, with a paused state while waiting on the customer.
items.docs: deadline and startedAt are the target and when its clock started; the line reads First response in 12 min (label is the words before the time, with the preposition: First response in, Resolve within; without it the line reads 12 min left), then Breached by 25 min once the deadline has passed. The state is written as well as styled: On track, At risk (when a quarter of the target is left, or thresholds says otherwise with atRiskFraction or atRiskMinutes), Breached and Paused, each with its own icon. pausedAt stops the clock and the line reads Paused: waiting on customer (change the reason with pausedReason). businessHours { days, start, end, timeZone } counts working time only, across clock changes, and shows hours rather than days. Time is worked out from timestamps and refreshed once a minute and when a sleeping tab wakes; the ticking is never announced, only a change of state is, politely and once. A thin bar shows how much of the target has gone (showProgress), and the tooltip, on hover, on focus and on a tap, gives the exact deadline. Pass now to get the words in server HTML, in tests and in previews; without it the server shows the due date until the clock is known. locale and timeZone format numbers and dates, labels translates every word.

items.name: attendee-list
items.title: Attendee list
items.description: Who is coming: attendees with their response, grouped counts and your own RSVP, for meetings and events.
items.docs: attendees is { id, name, email, image, response, optional } with a response of accepted, declined, tentative or none. The list opens with counts (4 yes, 1 maybe, 2 waiting, left out when zero) that are a polite status, so a change is read out, and a thin bar of the same shares. Each answer is written out as Accepted, Tentative, Declined or No response and drawn as a different shape, so none depends on colour. organizer and you are attendee ids: the organizer leads and carries a tag, you come next with three buttons (Yes, Maybe, No) that call onRespond and may return a promise, and only the organizer sees a Remind button on rows that have not answered, calling onRemind (also a promise: busy, then Reminded). maxVisible (default 5) folds the rest behind Show 12 more and never folds the organizer or you away. The row reads its own width: narrow, the answer moves under the name. headingLevel sets the heading (2 to 4) and labels translates every word.

items.name: task-relations
items.title: Task relations
items.description: Task dependencies in groups: blocked by, blocks and related, each with its status and an add-link action.
items.docs: relations is { blockedBy, blocks, related }, each a list of tasks { id, key, title, status, href } with a status of todo, in-progress, in-review, done or cancelled, drawn as a ring, a half ring, a three-quarter ring, a solid disc with a tick and a ring with a slash, and always written out. Empty groups are not drawn. A task with open blockers says so at the top (Blocked by 2 open tasks, a polite status) and its resolved blockers (done or cancelled) fold away behind Show 2 resolved. With canEdit, Add link opens a small searchable menu over candidates (those already linked are left out) with the kind of link to make; onAdd(kind, task) may return a promise: the picked row then shows a spinner, the rest wait and a second pick does nothing, and a rejection keeps the menu open and says so. Every row gets a remove button that asks first in a confirmation; onRemove(kind, task) may return a promise. Both are announced, and focus lands on the panel when a row disappears. onOpen(task, event) makes rows open: with href the title is a link and the event reaches your router, without it the row is a button. The panel reads its own width: narrow, the status moves under the title. headingLevel (2 to 4) sets the heading and the group names sit one level below. labels translates every word.

items.name: two-column-sign-in
items.title: Two-column sign-in
items.description: A full-page sign-in with the form on one side and a quiet brand panel with a customer quote on the other, folding to the form alone on a phone.
items.docs: onSubmit({ email, password, remember }) signs the person in: return a message to show it in one announced error region above the fields (That email and password do not match), or nothing when it worked; a thrown error shows a general message. The button is busy while it runs and a second submit is ignored, and what was typed survives a failed attempt (the password field is focused and selected so it can be retyped). A missing or malformed field is told under the field. providers is a slot above a labelled divider (dividerLabel) for single sign-on and passkey buttons, forgotHref adds the Forgot password link, brand is your logo, footer sits under the form, and titleAs is h1 (the default, when the form is the page) or h2. aside is the other column for a quote, a product shot or a photo: it is hidden below lg and decorative (hidden from assistive technology) unless you give it asideLabel, so a phone gets the form alone in a column no wider than 24rem. Its top edge is level with the form column's, so a row of your own that is 2.5rem high lines up with the brand. It uses semantic tokens only, with a hairline between the halves and no gradient behind the quote. heading, description, submitLabel and labels change the words.

items.name: magic-link-sign-in
items.title: Magic link sign-in
items.description: Passwordless sign-in: one email field, then an in-place check-your-inbox state with a timed resend and a way back to the form.
items.docs: onRequestLink({ email, remember }) asks your server to email the link. Resolve whether or not the address has an account, so the card never shows which addresses are registered (the confirmation says If the address has an account, a link is on its way); reject only when the request itself failed, and the card keeps the typed address and shows one retry message. A malformed address is caught when the field is left, with the message tied to the field. On success the card swaps in place to Check your inbox: it names the address, says the link works once for expiresInMinutes (default 15), says where to look, and offers Resend link, Use a different email and, with onUsePassword, Sign in with a password. The resend button counts down resendAfter seconds (default 30) in tabular figures, its name stays Resend link while it waits, and the status region speaks only when the wait starts and when it ends; the wait is worked out from timestamps, so it is right after the tab sleeps. Focus moves to the confirmation heading and back to the field. signedIn flips the card to You are signed in with a Continue button (onSignedIn) for apps that notice the link was opened in another tab. defaultEmail and defaultSent start on the confirmation, titleAs sets the heading element, footer sits under the card, labels translates every word.

items.name: passkey-sign-in
items.title: Passkey sign-in
items.description: A passkey-first sign-in: one large "Sign in with a passkey" button, autofill on the email field, and a quiet fallback to a password or a link.
items.docs: onPasskey({ email }) is yours: run WebAuthn in it (the block never touches navigator.credentials) and resolve when it is done; email is what was typed in the field and may be empty. While the browser prompt is open the big button reads Waiting for your device with a spinner and the same press cannot run twice (busy forces that state for a redirect or a preview). Report what went wrong through error: cancelled, not-found or unsupported each become plain words with the next step, announced once (a rejection with no error set shows a general message; labels.errors translates them). supported={false} removes the button and the field and leads with the fallbacks as full buttons. fallbacks are { id, label, href or onSelect }, shown as quiet text actions under the field (Use a password instead, Email me a link). The email field has autocomplete=username webauthn, so the browser can offer a saved passkey in it, and pressing Enter in it runs the same sign-in. A one-line explanation of what a passkey is sits behind a term, the word passkey with a dotted underline that opens a small named panel on click, tap or Enter (labels.lead, term and definition). Targets are 44px and up (the word passkey is a link inside a sentence, with a padded hit area), the fingerprint tile is a monochrome circle, and nothing depends on a pointer. titleAs sets the heading element, footer sits under the card.
